**Graphics.** Claude can now see your ROM's sprites, palettes and maps, and edit the art.

### New tools

- **`view_image`** shows any sprite, tileset, tilemap or palette as an image the assistant can see, drawn with its palette the way HMA shows it. It works by name (`graphics.pokemon.sprites.front`, row `CHARMANDER`) and also covers:
  - shiny palettes (`palette=graphics.pokemon.palettes.shiny`)
  - overworld sprites and all their frames
  - icons, trainer sprites and the title screen
  - `save_to`, which writes a PNG you can edit in any art program, keeping the sprite's palette.
- **`import_image`** puts an edited PNG back using HMA's own image import. When other sprites share the palette, you choose how to handle it: `smart` (the default) balances the palette for all of them, `greedy` rewrites it for this image, and `cautious` keeps it and matches your colors to it. A PNG saved by `view_image` goes back with its exact colors. Importing an image identical to what's there writes nothing. Compressed sprites that grow are moved and repointed.
- **`read_palette` / `write_palette`** show and change a palette's colors as `#RRGGBB`, and list which graphics use it.
- **`render_map`** draws a map as HMA's map editor shows it, with or without NPCs and event markers. Each block is 16×16 pixels, matching the coordinates from `map_events`.

### Try

- *"Show me Charmander's shiny sprite, then make its flame blue."*
- *"Draw Pallet Town with its NPCs."*
- *"Save Pikachu's front sprite as a PNG so I can edit it, then import my version."*

### Known limits

- An imported image must be the same size as the graphic it replaces.
- Map tiles can't be edited yet. That's next.
- Editing a compressed sprite usually moves it to free space, because HMA's compressor packs slightly less tightly than the original game's. Pointers are updated, and the result tells you when it moved.

Tested on FireRed (U) 1.0 and Emerald (U). See [docs/limitations.md](https://github.com/dewayneku/hma-mcp/blob/main/docs/limitations.md) for everything else.

### Download

| You use | Get |
|---|---|
| Claude Desktop | `hma-mcp-win32.mcpb`, `hma-mcp-darwin.mcpb` (Apple Silicon) or `hma-mcp-linux.mcpb`, then double-click it |
| Claude Code, other clients | `hma-mcp-<system>.zip` / `.tar.gz`; unpack and point your client at `hma-mcp` ([setup](https://github.com/dewayneku/hma-mcp#quick-start)) |

The builds are self-contained, so you don't need .NET. On macOS, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine <folder>` on a downloaded build before starting it.
